nodes.label: NOTE: unlike serializeForm, populateForm fills disabled elements too,
nodes.norm_label: note: unlike serializeform, populateform fills disabled elements too,

nodes.label: Pitfall: CamelCase Dataset Keys vs Underscored Names
nodes.norm_label: pitfall: camelcase dataset keys vs underscored names
nodes.rationale: data-ln-fill-max-users maps to maxUsers in the JS dataset; if the input name uses underscores, data-ln-fill-as must be supplied to match.

nodes.label: Pitfall: Hidden Input Required for Checkboxes
nodes.norm_label: pitfall: hidden input required for checkboxes
nodes.rationale: Standalone checkboxes submit nothing when unchecked, so a hidden input with the false value must precede them.

nodes.label: Row Actions Rule (Always Visible, No Hover-Only)
nodes.norm_label: row actions rule (always visible, no hover-only)
nodes.rationale: Hover-only actions are excluded because touch devices exist and cannot hover.

nodes.label: Windowed Sliding-Cache Exception
nodes.rationale: For datasets too large to cache entirely client-side, a bounded sliding window (opt-in) replaces the full cache while sort/filter/search still resolve against the full dataset, computed server-side instead.

nodes.label: Component Ownership and Isolation in the Write Pipeline
nodes.norm_label: component ownership and isolation in the write pipeline
nodes.rationale: ln-form owns action/method, ln-validate owns the submit gate, ln-data-store owns the cache, ln-api-queue owns persistence order, connectors own transport, and the coordinator mediates — each stays blind to the others' concerns.

nodes.label: Scenario 4: Handling 409 Conflicts (Server Wins)
nodes.rationale: 409 is classified as deterministic — the server's record overwrites the local cache and the outbox entry is dropped to prevent endless retries.

nodes.label: Scenario 2: Editing a Record via lnFill (PUT/PATCH)
nodes.norm_label: scenario 2: editing a record via lnfill (put/patch)

nodes.label: Scenario 3: Offline Edits and Persistent Queuing
nodes.norm_label: scenario 3: offline edits and persistent queuing

nodes.label: Filter Anatomy: Icon → ln-popover → ln-search + ul
nodes.norm_label: filter anatomy: icon → ln-popover → ln-search + ul

nodes.label: Filter Options Come From Domain Source, Never Data
nodes.norm_label: filter options come from domain source, never data
nodes.rationale: Options are authored markup from the domain enum so the same markup serves SSR and SPA identically, rather than being derived from currently displayed rows.

nodes.label: Scope Boundaries: Record-Backed vs Filter Context
nodes.norm_label: scope boundaries: record-backed vs filter context

nodes.label: Selection Control Ladder (≤5/6-10/≥11)
nodes.rationale: No custom select component exists by design; the domain enum's option count (never the rows currently in data) picks between inline pills, a plain popover, or a popover with ln-search.

nodes.label: CSS/JS Hook Boundary
nodes.rationale: Bare functional JS attribute presence must never be styled directly; only specific state values may be styled, to avoid selector collisions and specificity bugs.

nodes.label: Helper-Class Convention (P1)
nodes.rationale: Unprefixed helper classes are thin visual mixin bindings; state classes are forbidden because JS component state must live exclusively in data-ln-* attributes, never queried via CSS classes.

nodes.label: Visibility and Hiding Doctrine (P4)
nodes.rationale: Native [hidden] attribute plus a co-located (0,2,0)-specificity selector unconditionally overrides un-scoped external utility classes (e.g. Tailwind at 0,1,0) without global class hacks; .ln-hidden does not exist.

nodes.label: Z-Index and Top-Layer Stacking
nodes.rationale: Modals/dropdowns/popovers are promoted to the browser top layer, stacking by most-recently-shown order, immune to ancestor stacking contexts, so no CSS z-index coordination is needed between them.

nodes.label: Dark Mode / Theming via Vocabulary Rebinding
nodes.norm_label: dark mode / theming via vocabulary rebinding
nodes.rationale: Rebinding vocabulary tokens at theme root scope (never nested descendant selectors) lets component mixins shift globally without per-component overrides.

nodes.label: The Four Token Layers (Brand/Scale/Vocabulary/Primitive)
nodes.rationale: Each layer is not interchangeable even though all resolve to CSS values; separation lets themes/modes/skins rebind vocabulary without touching mixins that read only primitives.

nodes.label: Freeze Rule Invariant
nodes.rationale: Accent-derived interaction states are tokenised as ratio percentages rather than pre-resolved :root colors so color-mix() executes at the local declaration site and resolves dynamically on the component cascade.

nodes.label: Own-the-Pair Rule
nodes.rationale: An element rebinding --color-bg must also paint --color-fg in the same rule; otherwise text colour inherits from an arbitrary ancestor and contrast against a self-chosen surface cannot be guaranteed.

nodes.label: The Rebind Contract (Read vs Write Boundaries)
nodes.norm_label: the rebind contract (read vs write boundaries)
nodes.rationale: Mixins read primitives only; components rebind primitives locally to select a vocabulary role; themes/modes/skins rebind vocabulary at root scope — keeps concerns from leaking across layers.

nodes.label: API Export Patterns (global constructor / element API / global listener)
nodes.norm_label: api export patterns (global constructor / element api / global listener)

nodes.label: Template System (HTML structure, zero display text in JS)
nodes.norm_label: template system (html structure, zero display text in js)

nodes.label: IIFE Component Encapsulation
nodes.rationale: Paired selectors (data-ln-{name} <-> el.ln{Name}) keep instances DOM-bound rather than in a global registry, letting multiple instances coexist safely on one page.

nodes.label: Async Cancellation & No-Destroyed-Event Invariant (P2)
nodes.rationale: Every async-performing component must hold an AbortController and abort in-flight work on destroy(); a destroyed component must not mutate DOM or dispatch any event, including a teardown/:destroyed event, because no destroyed lifecycle event exists in the framework.

nodes.label: The destroy() Contract (P3)
nodes.rationale: Governing test: would this exist in the DOM if the component had never executed? destroy() must remove everything it created, including traces on foreign elements, except authored attributes whose value it merely changed.

nodes.label: Windowed Sliding-Window Virtualization (createWindowCache)
nodes.rationale: Opt-in server-side sliding-window cache (windowSize/pageSize/threshold) shared identically by ln-list and ln-table: stamps resident rows, requests missing pages via offset/limit/queryGen, LRU-evicts beyond windowSize, and drops stale responses by queryGen mismatch. Exists so very large datasets can be browsed without holding the full set in memory or DOM, while per-row selection still survives eviction.

nodes.label: Two-Host Attribute Bridge Pattern
nodes.rationale: Splits a primitive into a Control role (captures user input, writes a state attribute onto a separate target) and a State Host role (owns the attribute as single source of truth, dispatches a cancelable change event, runs a default DOM behaviour unless a consumer calls preventDefault()). Avoids direct JS references between control and target, letting any number of controls/consumers coordinate purely through attributes and one cancelable event contract; ln-sort explicitly follows the same contract shape as ln-search.

nodes.label: CSS-Driven Sort Cycle State Machine
nodes.rationale: The none→asc→desc→none cycle is produced entirely by CSS selecting on the root's data-ln-sort-state attribute (only one data-ln-sort-dir button visible at a time); JS only reads the clicked button's direction and writes the state attribute. Keeps JS free of cycle/branching logic and keeps state observable in the attribute rather than in class toggling, per the project's state-in-attribute doctrine.

nodes.label: tooltip (CSS-only pseudo-element)
nodes.rationale: data-ln-tooltip is a visual hint only, not an accessible-name replacement; no viewport collision detection, so interactive/collision-aware needs escalate to the JS ln-tooltip or ln-popover.

nodes.label: Template Syntax Decision Matrix
nodes.rationale: {{ field }} and data-ln-table-cell-attr run once at clone time via fillTemplate/_fillRow; data-ln-field re-runs on every fill() call. Placing data-ln-field inside a cloned row template is a silent no-op (the Row Template Trap) because the renderer never calls fill() on cloned rows.

nodes.label: Behavior Is Attached, Not Owned (Principle 3)
nodes.rationale: Autonomous IIFE components bind via data-ln-*, auto-init via MutationObserver, and communicate via CustomEvents addressed by element id, making DOM position irrelevant to wiring — teleport-safe by design.

nodes.label: Forced X-LN-Response: data header
nodes.rationale: Forced on every verb via one internal helper so it can't be removed or overridden; backend uses it to select JSON data mode and it doubles as a CSRF guard.

nodes.label: Connector- and ID-Blind by Design
nodes.rationale: The queue never imports/references a connector and never distinguishes a temp id from a real id except as an opaque string; all transport execution and id semantics live in the coordinator/connector.

nodes.label: Mutation Response Envelope
nodes.rationale: Mirrors ln-api-connector's {message,content} contract so a proxy/gateway placed in front of raw CouchDB can opt into success toasts, while direct CouchDB (which never sends the envelope) stays toast-silent and JS callers see an unchanged resolve shape.

nodes.label: Offline Outbox Write Routing
nodes.rationale: When an ln-api-queue child is present every write is enqueued instead of hitting the connector directly, giving at-least-once delivery via an Idempotency-Key without changing the write intake contract.

nodes.label: Three-Layer Architecture (Coordinator/Component/Library)
nodes.rationale: Separating coordinator/component/library keeps components storage-agnostic and sibling-agnostic; changing the backend or adding a component requires changes only in the coordinator.

nodes.label: Visual/Functional Attribute Separation
nodes.rationale: data-ln-* is strictly a JS binding hook and must never be used as a bare CSS selector for presentation, keeping behavior wiring and visual styling independently changeable.

nodes.label: Semantic Class Naming (No BEM, No Utility Classes)
nodes.norm_label: semantic class naming (no bem, no utility classes)
nodes.rationale: Utility class chains and BEM compounds are forbidden because layouts/styles must be compiled and maintained in SCSS via mixin binding to semantic class or id selectors, not hacked in markup; state/variant classes name the domain, not the tone.

nodes.label: Component vs Coordinator Rule (CQS)
nodes.rationale: Components never open modals/toasts/read foreign forms; coordinators never call state-mutation prototype methods directly (e.g. el.lnProfile.create() is forbidden) and must dispatch sanctioned events instead — enforcing command/query separation between wiring and state.

nodes.label: Shared Resource Pools and Caching
nodes.rationale: Components requiring ticks share one module-level setInterval iterating a registered Set rather than each instantiating its own timer; expensive Intl formatters are cached globally by locale+options key.

nodes.label: Cloned Templates and Declarative Data Fills
nodes.norm_label: cloned templates and declarative data fills
nodes.rationale: Components must never build UI via innerHTML strings or createElement chains; DOM structures come from authored <template> markup only.

nodes.label: Localization and the Dictionary Pattern
nodes.rationale: JS files must not hardcode user-facing strings so translation stays authorable in HTML markup rather than JS source.

nodes.label: Action-Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: USER ACTION -> SYSTEM ACKNOWLEDGES -> SYSTEM PROCESSES -> SYSTEM RESPONDS -> NEXT STATE. Missing any step breaks the interaction: no acknowledge means the user doesn't know the click registered, no processing indicator invites a double action, no response leaves the outcome unknown, no next state leaves the user without a path forward.

nodes.label: Destructive Action Confirmation Ladder
nodes.rationale: Three patterns scaled to risk: no confirmation (instant, reversible — toggle off, remove filter), inline confirm (double-click, auto-reverts after a timeout — single-row delete in a list), modal confirm (irreversible/cascading/bulk 5+ — explain consequences and count). Only destructive actions confirm; confirming everything teaches users to click through blind. Labels are descriptive actions, never OK/Cancel.

nodes.label: Standard Edge-Case Catalog For Data Views
nodes.norm_label: standard edge-case catalog for data views
nodes.rationale: First use, one item, 1000+ items, very long text/names, slow network, offline, double click, browser back, refresh mid-form, mobile screen, concurrent edit (last write wins, indicated). Every feature should have an explicit design answer for each.

nodes.label: Two Distinct Empty-State Types
nodes.rationale: Type 1 — no data exists (onboarding moment: heading + message + primary CTA to create), appears only once. Type 2 — query returned zero (search/filter/view active, guide to clear it). Using the wrong type confuses users; never show a blank area for either.

nodes.label: Error Recovery Design
nodes.rationale: Match error to scope: field error -> inline, action error -> toast, page error -> full-page state. Always offer a next step (retry, fix, go back). Human language, never a raw status code or exception string. Progress and form data survive errors; a failing section degrades gracefully without breaking the rest of the page.

nodes.label: Filter Interaction Pattern
nodes.rationale: Column filter dropdown with checkbox list; filters AND together across columns and combine (AND) with search; active-filter dot indicator plus sticky-footer pills with a Clear-all action; filter options come from the domain source, never derived from the visible page dataset.

nodes.label: Four-State View Machine (LOADING/EMPTY/OK/ERROR)
nodes.rationale: Every data-driven view is a state machine with exactly four states. Loading: scoped indicator, nothing clickable. Empty: explanation + next action (two distinct sub-types: no data yet vs query returned zero). OK: data + actions. Error: human-readable cause + a recovery path. Designing only the OK state is an incomplete feature.

nodes.label: Inline Editing Pattern
nodes.rationale: Click editable cell -> input with original value pre-filled and focused; Enter/Tab validates and optimistically saves, Tab moves to the next editable cell, Escape reverts and exits. Single-cell edit only, never a whole-row edit mode. Use inline for quick single-field corrections across many rows; use a form/modal for multi-field or dependent-field edits.

nodes.label: Keyboard Navigation Rules
nodes.rationale: / focuses search (no input active); Escape closes/cancels; table arrow keys move row focus, Enter opens, Space toggles checkbox; modals trap focus (Tab/Shift+Tab cycle inside, never reach the page behind); no keyboard traps anywhere; composite widgets use arrow keys internally.

nodes.label: Motion Is Communication, Not Decoration
nodes.rationale: Animate appear/disappear, expand/collapse, hover/focus feedback, and loading-state progress because the user needs to track what changed. Never scroll-triggered in data tools, never blocking, always honoring prefers-reduced-motion.

nodes.label: Multi-Step Process Design
nodes.rationale: Use only for 3+ distinct phases with dependent data; show progress, allow back without losing data, validate per step, add a review step, single submit at the final step. Not for simple forms under 10 fields or independent fields.

nodes.label: Navigation Flow Rules
nodes.rationale: Create -> detail of the new item; edit+save -> stay with feedback or back to detail; delete from list -> stay on list; delete from detail -> back to list; cancel -> back with no confirmation. URLs reflect state and are bookmarkable; back never loses data; returning to a list preserves search, filters, sort and scroll.

nodes.label: Row Actions Click-Zone Pattern
nodes.rationale: Row click (outside action buttons) navigates to detail as the default action; action buttons stop propagation; actions stay always-visible rather than hover-revealed (inaccessible on touch); 3+ actions collapse into an overflow menu; row/action click wiring should be declarative data-attributes, not JS click handlers.

nodes.label: Row Selection + Bulk Actions Pattern
nodes.rationale: Header checkbox scope is the currently visible/filtered rows only, with an optional 'select all N' banner for the full dataset; sticky bulk-action bar; destructive bulk actions always confirm with a modal and a count; partial failure reports a breakdown (e.g. '2 deleted, 3 failed').

nodes.label: Search Interaction Pattern
nodes.rationale: Instant on keyup for client-cached data (no debounce needed, Array.filter is synchronous); debounce only when search hits a server endpoint. Clear button, preserve term on back-navigation, / keyboard shortcut, two distinct empty states (no data exists vs zero results).

nodes.label: Sort Interaction Pattern (Three-State Cycle)
nodes.rationale: Unsorted -> ascending -> descending -> unsorted. Single-column sort only; visual indicator always visible (dim unsorted, bold active); instant client-side, no loading indicator; preserved across back-navigation.

nodes.label: Toast Feedback Channel Rules
nodes.rationale: Success/info auto-dismiss, warning auto-dismiss with a longer duration, error persists until dismissed. Content is short, specific, past tense, never technical. Position: bottom-right desktop, full-width anchored to the bottom edge on mobile.

nodes.label: Virtual Scroll Pattern (vs Pagination)
nodes.rationale: Continuous scroll over the full dataset instead of artificial page boundaries; sticky header/footer; shimmer on initial load, never a blank table; scroll position preserved on back-navigation. Windowed exception: for datasets too large to cache client-side, ln-core.createWindowCache (opt-in via data-ln-table-window / data-ln-list-window) swaps the full local cache for a bounded resident window that round-trips pages to the server as the user scrolls — the feel is unchanged, only the implementation trades a full cache for a sliding window.

nodes.label: UX Interaction Rules Skill
nodes.rationale: Governs HOW an interface behaves: action-feedback loop, four-state machine, feedback channels, navigation flow, destructive-action confirmation, multi-step process design, error recovery, edge cases, motion, anti-patterns. Companion to ui.md (visual layout) and ux-interaction-patterns.md (concrete flows).

nodes.label: UX Flows Skill
nodes.rationale: Condensed sibling of ux.md: action-feedback loop, four states, feedback strategy, navigation, destructive-action ladder, error recovery, edge cases, keyboard, motion, anti-patterns.

nodes.label: UX Interaction Patterns Skill
nodes.rationale: Concrete FLOW definitions for the recurring data-driven interactions of a business UI: search, sort, filter, virtual scroll, row selection/bulk actions, inline editing, keyboard navigation, empty states, row actions. Explicit companion to ux.md.

nodes.label: Mixin Architecture (Primitives vs Composites)
nodes.rationale: Divides SCSS into zero-selector atomic primitives and full semantic component recipes so mixins bind to stable selectors instead of utility class bloat in HTML.

nodes.label: Auto-Flush Table Embedding
nodes.rationale: :has(> table:only-child) strips outer padding/duplicate borders only when the table is the sole child, preserving normal padding when text accompanies the table.

nodes.label: badge / status-badge
nodes.rationale: Colored status dot plus text label avoids color-only communication; .live pulse respects prefers-reduced-motion.

nodes.label: table-base (data table styling)
nodes.rationale: Global baseline applies sunken header, row hover, tabular numerals automatically; sticky/striped are explicit mixin opt-ins.

nodes.label: Scoped Mode/Theme Islands
nodes.rationale: data-mode/data-theme/data-skin can be declared at any DOM depth so descendants fully re-theme without component-specific overrides, decoupling raw palette values from the derivation chain.

nodes.label: Zero-Specificity Default Values (:where())
nodes.rationale: Defaults declared with :where(:root)/:where([data-mode]) sit at specificity (0,0,0) so a consumer brand.css at :root always wins regardless of stylesheet load order.

nodes.label: Contrast Budget Constants
nodes.rationale: Three build-time SCSS constants ($ln-contrast-text 7:1, $ln-contrast-fill 7:1, $ln-contrast-ui 3:1) drive lightness solves so contrast is engineered rather than eyeballed.

nodes.label: Shared MutationObserver Auto-Initialization
nodes.rationale: One shared observer on document.body with no per-name filter delivers every data-ln-* mutation; an echo guard skips same-value writes and components never install their own filtered observer, so a developer can bootstrap a component live from DevTools.

nodes.label: State Tiers & Scope of §1 (P5)
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes public control state (DOM attributes, fully in scope), application data (ln-data-store/IndexedDB, out of scope), operational mechanics (JS memory, never mirrored as attributes), and ln-core helpers (no host, not applicable).

nodes.label: The Two-Host Pattern (Control vs State Host)
nodes.norm_label: the two-host pattern (control vs state host)
nodes.rationale: The control/trigger element never mutates target state directly in JS — it writes the target's DOM attribute; the state host owns the true state and reacts through the shared attribute observer, keeping trigger and target decoupled.

nodes.label: Contrast Budget for a Custom Brand
nodes.norm_label: contrast budget for a custom brand
nodes.rationale: Shipped presets solve lightness to 7:1 at build time against the nearer foreground pole; a runtime brand.css rebind is invisible to that solve, so the library documents per-hue lightness ceilings (white vs ink) rather than guaranteeing contrast for arbitrary custom brands.

nodes.label: Surface Elevation Inversion
nodes.rationale: In dark mode elevated surfaces go lighter than the root canvas (recessed areas darker) because the three --fg-* tiers need luminance headroom to clear 7:1; raising the surfaces would collapse that ladder. Light mode stays flat, separated by shadow instead.

nodes.label: Attribute Bridge Pattern (DOM as Control Plane)
nodes.norm_label: attribute bridge pattern (dom as control plane)
nodes.rationale: Core axiom: the DOM is the public/observable state surface while JS holds implementation state and local-first data, so any UI control state can be authored, inspected, or restored from HTML attributes alone.

nodes.label: Why the Checkbox Hack Is Forbidden
nodes.norm_label: why the checkbox hack is forbidden
nodes.rationale: Programmatically setting .checked=true does not fire native input/change events nor MutationObserver attribute watches, it breaks encapsulation, and it violates ARIA accessibility standards.

nodes.label: State in Attribute, Never in Class (P1)
nodes.norm_label: state in attribute, never in class (p1)
nodes.rationale: Both bare state classes (.open, .active) and prefixed ones (.ln-chart--loading) are forbidden; mutually exclusive states use a valued attribute, independent booleans use bare attribute presence, keeping CSS classes purely presentational.

nodes.label: Visibility and Hiding Doctrine (P4)
nodes.rationale: Uses native hidden property/attribute paired with a host-scoped [data-ln-component][hidden]{display:none!important} SCSS rule at (0,2,0) specificity, reliably beating external framework utilities like Tailwind's 0,1,0 flex without global .ln-hidden class collisions.

nodes.label: HTML-First Swapping philosophy
nodes.rationale: The server remains the single source of truth for data and markup; the client swaps selector-mapped HTML fragments instead of client routers rendering JSON.

nodes.label: AJAX Fragment Trust Boundary
nodes.rationale: ln-ajax performs no client-side sanitization because that would be fragile and could corrupt valid markup (e.g. stripping data-ln-confirm values); sanitizing user-submitted HTML is the server's job.

nodes.label: Local-first write routing (data-ln-form-scope)
nodes.rationale: A scoped form's submit can be claimed at exactly one of three rungs (native, ln-ajax, or the nearest ln-data-coordinator), so the same markup supports SSR, progressive-enhancement ajax, and local-first write pipelines without ln-form itself knowing which applies.

nodes.label: 3-Tier Data Layer Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Nesting coordinator > store > connector > queue in the DOM isolates storage caches from transport protocols; the store is blind to REST endpoints and the connector is agnostic to schemas.

nodes.label: Ingress/Egress Data Mapper Registry
nodes.rationale: Inline <script data-ln-mapper> mappers were deprecated and disabled because executable script in HTML attributes violates CSP and relies on unsafe eval/new Function vulnerable to XSS; mappers must be registered via registerDataMapper in compiled JS modules instead.

nodes.label: lnFill Region Filling Helper
nodes.rationale: Fills form inputs and display elements together from one record via declarative data-ln-fill-* triggers; nested fillable components must guard on e.target!==this.dom to avoid double-triggering from bubbled events.

nodes.label: Interactive Element Tag Rules
nodes.rationale: Buttons for page-local mutations, anchors only for navigation; binding clicks to div/span/li/td bypasses native keyboard nav and breaks screen readers.

nodes.label: ul/li Dictionary Pattern (i18n)
nodes.rationale: Hardcoding user-facing strings in JS is forbidden; translation strings live in a hidden ul with data-ln-{component}-dict li items, read once via buildDict() at init, keeping localized text authored in HTML rather than buried in JS.

nodes.label: WCAG 2.2 AA Design Target + AAA Contrast
nodes.norm_label: wcag 2.2 aa design target + aaa contrast
nodes.rationale: Full AAA conformance turns on criteria a component library cannot determine (reading level, sign language, context help), so the library commits to AA as engineering target but settles contrast at AAA (1.4.6) since contrast is fully decided by shipped palette values.

nodes.label: No Bare <div> Doctrine
nodes.rationale: Prioritizing native semantic HTML5 tags over generic divs keeps ln-ashlar server-renderable, accessible by default, and easy to inspect; repeating siblings of the same type must use ul/li or ol/li, never adjacent divs/spans.

nodes.label: Frozen Attributes Convention
nodes.rationale: A constructor-only attribute that cannot be re-read at runtime (e.g. an IndexedDB schema fixed at open time) surfaces post-init edits via a data-ln-{component}-frozen self-attribute and a *-dev.scss dev-dom-error affordance under [data-ln-debug], never via console.warn.

nodes.label: Composition Over Features (Principle 5)
nodes.rationale: A filterable table is popover+search+filter composed together rather than a monolithic table with built-in filter UI; big components expose events instead of growing features.

nodes.label: Core Owns All Standard Compositions (Principle 8)
nodes.rationale: A consumer project needing a local SCSS patch for a standard composition is treated as a doctrine violation, since per-project patches scatter fixes and diverge into tech debt over time.

nodes.label: CSS Owns All Presentation Including States (Principle 4)
nodes.norm_label: css owns all presentation including states (principle 4)
nodes.rationale: JS only toggles .ln-* state classes or semantic attributes; CSS translates those to visual output so a design token change propagates without hunting JS files.

nodes.label: Declarative Wiring Over Coordinators (Principle 10)
nodes.rationale: A trigger declares an entire flow (open modal, fill form, set title) via attributes so the behavior is inspectable in DevTools instead of hidden in coordinator JS; rule of thumb is click-triggered flows go declarative, programmatic flows (conflict resolution, deep-link pre-fill) still use a coordinator calling lnFill.

nodes.label: Domain Truth Lives at the Source (Principle 6)
nodes.norm_label: domain truth lives at the source (principle 6)
nodes.rationale: Filter options must come from the domain owner (backend enum/lookup table), not be derived from the visible dataset, since dataset derivation breaks under pagination and hides valid domain states with zero current records.

nodes.label: Case Study — The Filter-Clipping Saga (Principle 11)
nodes.rationale: Three divergent filter-dropdown implementations kept re-patching an overflow-clipping symptom because JS was generating UI chrome in-tree; the cure was static authored ln-popover markup teleported to body, collapsing three code paths into one pattern and removing ~145 lines from ln-table.

nodes.label: Honest Ledger — Strengths and Costs
nodes.rationale: Judges ln-ashlar against its own contract (markup owns structure, CSS owns presentation, events own communication) rather than against a virtual-DOM framework's; wins include zero-hydration authored HTML and closed-taxonomy offline writes, costs include no compile-time type safety and no static who-listens-to-what graph.

nodes.label: Lean JS — Misuse Is a CSS Affordance, Not a Console Warning (Principle 9)
nodes.norm_label: lean js — misuse is a css affordance, not a console warning (principle 9)
nodes.rationale: Developer misuse surfaces via a red CSS ::after affordance in dev mode rather than console.warn, because console warnings disappear unnoticed while an on-page label is impossible to miss and costs nothing in production.

nodes.label: Markup Is the Application (Principle 1)
nodes.rationale: HTML is authored, complete and semantic; JS never generates UI chrome, so the interface is server-renderable, inspectable, and free of FOUC on chrome — <template> exists only for data-driven row repetition.

nodes.label: Raw vs Formatted — Never Sort/Filter Displayed Text (Principle 7)
nodes.norm_label: raw vs formatted — never sort/filter displayed text (principle 7)
nodes.rationale: data-ln-value and data-ln-filter-value carry machine values because formatted text like "$1,234.56" or "● Active" is not correctly sortable or matchable as text.

nodes.label: SSR and SPA Share Identical Markup (Principle 2)
nodes.norm_label: ssr and spa share identical markup (principle 2)
nodes.rationale: Only the data source differs between SSR and data-driven pages; structure stays identical, eliminating hydration cost and structure mismatch.

nodes.label: Templates Are Authored Markup (Principle 12)
nodes.rationale: A <template> is page-authored markup the library clones for runtime data — never a library-shipped hidden default injected via innerHTML — so a missing template fails loudly with a console warning instead of a silent fallback.

nodes.label: Component Isolation and Wrapper-Level Scoping Rules
nodes.norm_label: component isolation and wrapper-level scoping rules

nodes.label: Command and Query Separation (CQS) Rules
nodes.rationale: Coordinators must never call state-mutation prototype methods directly, to prevent tight coupling between coordinators and components.

nodes.label: The Four Responsibilities of a Coordinator
nodes.norm_label: the four responsibilities of a coordinator

nodes.label: Local DOM Scoping (No document.querySelectorAll)
nodes.rationale: Scoping selectors to the coordinator's local DOM subtree lets multiple instances run concurrently on one page without ID or resource collisions.

nodes.label: Normalizing Surfaces at the Open Boundary
nodes.norm_label: normalizing surfaces at the open boundary
nodes.rationale: Panels/drawers/modals persist in the DOM and are reused across records, so they must be reset before opening (not on close) to avoid accumulating residual state.

nodes.label: ARIA APG Keyboard Navigation
nodes.rationale: Implements the ARIA Authoring Practices menu pattern (roving tabindex, Home/End, Escape, Tab) so authors get compliant keyboard semantics without annotating children manually.

nodes.label: Orthogonality design principle
nodes.rationale: Splits state (ln-toggle), behavior/positioning (JS), and visuals (CSS) into three layers instead of one heavy bundled component, so each concern can be replaced independently.

nodes.label: Presentation Coordinator pattern
nodes.rationale: Dropdown never manages open/close state itself — it reacts to ln-toggle events and layers positioning/lifecycle behavior on top of a state primitive.

nodes.label: Top-layer promotion via Popover API
nodes.rationale: popover="manual" plus showPopover() escapes ancestor overflow:hidden clipping and stacking contexts without moving the menu in the DOM, while keeping dismissal under the component's own control.

nodes.label: defineAttrs(instance, dom, spec)
nodes.rationale: Getter-only properties that read the DOM live, on every access — nothing is copied into instance state, so a drifting copy is structurally impossible.

nodes.label: Frozen-attribute convention
nodes.rationale: A constructor-only attribute cannot physically be re-read at runtime (e.g. an IndexedDB schema fixed at open time); editing it after init is surfaced as a CSS-only dev affordance instead of silently ignored or console.warn'd.

nodes.label: Coordinator Mindset (zero internal state)
nodes.rationale: ln-accordion carries zero internal state; it only coordinates ln-toggle panels via attribute writes, keeping the toggle primitive oblivious to accordion membership.

nodes.label: loader (CSS spinner mixin)
nodes.rationale: Pure CSS pseudo-element spinner scaling via em/font-size avoids SVG/image asset dependencies and inherits --color-primary automatically.

nodes.label: motion-safe (reduced-motion gating)
nodes.rationale: Spatial transforms/keyframes are gated behind prefers-reduced-motion to prevent vestibular discomfort, while subtle color/background transitions stay active for interactive feedback.

nodes.label: page-header (:has() slot layout)
nodes.rationale: CSS-only Grid + :has() slot detection for breadcrumb/title/actions avoids JS-driven layout composition.

nodes.label: prose (editorial typography)
nodes.rationale: Restores bullets/blockquotes/rhythm for editorial content and constrains width to 65ch reading measure; kept opt-in so structural UI lists stay unstyled by default.

nodes.label: stat-card (KPI metric card)
nodes.rationale: Tabular numerals prevent layout shift on rapidly updating KPI values; directional trend indicators pair color with descriptive text.

nodes.label: stepper (sequential progress)
nodes.rationale: Ordered list with CSS counter() numbering so assistive tech announces total/sequential steps; aria-current=step marks the active node.

nodes.label: pills / pills-outline / pills-segmented / pills-switch
nodes.rationale: All four visual treatments share one symmetric ul>li>label>input structure over native checkbox/radio inputs so keyboard nav and AT compatibility are preserved; checkbox-hack disclosure widgets are forbidden in favor of ln-toggle.

nodes.label: Structural Lists vs Editorial Prose
nodes.rationale: UI lists (menus, tabs, chips) default to list-style:none/no padding; bullets/numbering/rhythm are opt-in via .prose so structural and editorial content never share unwanted styling.

nodes.label: Semantic Typography Roles
nodes.rationale: typography($role) rebinds --font-size/--line-height per semantic role so type scales with density tiers automatically, instead of hardcoded per-element sizes.

nodes.label: Three-Stage Accessibility Verification Workflow
nodes.rationale: Automated scans (axe/WAVE/Lighthouse) only detect a subset of WCAG criteria, so keyboard-only and screen-reader passes remain mandatory rather than optional add-ons.

nodes.label: Motion only for entrance/state-change/loading/feedback; animate only transform+opacity; respect prefers-reduced-motion
nodes.norm_label: motion only for entrance/state-change/loading/feedback; animate only transform+opacity; respect prefers-reduced-motion

nodes.label: Four hierarchy levels (primary/secondary/ghost/destructive); one primary per context; disabled is not a validation substitute
nodes.norm_label: four hierarchy levels (primary/secondary/ghost/destructive); one primary per context; disabled is not a validation substitute

nodes.label: Color communicates state, never decoration; never use a custom color outside the token set
nodes.norm_label: color communicates state, never decoration; never use a custom color outside the token set

nodes.label: Top-aligned labels default; field state ladder; error requires 3 signals (color+icon+text) below field; reserved error space; button positioning rules
nodes.norm_label: top-aligned labels default; field state ladder; error requires 3 signals (color+icon+text) below field; reserved error space; button positioning rules

nodes.label: All icons from the same set and stroke weight; never mix libraries or outline/filled variants
nodes.norm_label: all icons from the same set and stroke weight; never mix libraries or outline/filled variants

nodes.label: Default/hover/active/focus/disabled states consistent; hover = color change only, no transform/shadow
nodes.norm_label: default/hover/active/focus/disabled states consistent; hover = color change only, no transform/shadow

nodes.label: Backdrop+surface elevation both required; destructive confirm dialog grammar; inline confirmation as lower-overhead alternative; no modal stacking
nodes.norm_label: backdrop+surface elevation both required; destructive confirm dialog grammar; inline confirmation as lower-overhead alternative; no modal stacking

nodes.label: Three nav indicator types (background fill/bar/color-only); active always dominates hover; never mix types within one interface
nodes.norm_label: three nav indicator types (background fill/bar/color-only); active always dominates hover; never mix types within one interface

nodes.label: Rounded corners imply floating (need margin); sharp corners imply structure (flush); one standard radius + full rounding reserved for pills
nodes.norm_label: rounded corners imply floating (need margin); sharp corners imply structure (flush); one standard radius + full rounding reserved for pills

nodes.label: Container-first responsive; three semantic breakpoints (sm/md/lg) per component; viewport queries reserved for layout shell decisions
nodes.norm_label: container-first responsive; three semantic breakpoints (sm/md/lg) per component; viewport queries reserved for layout shell decisions

nodes.label: Shadow implies elevation, border implies containment — pick one as the primary signal
nodes.norm_label: shadow implies elevation, border implies containment — pick one as the primary signal

nodes.label: Never invent spacing values — use the token scale; arbitrary values signal a different root problem
nodes.norm_label: never invent spacing values — use the token scale; arbitrary values signal a different root problem

nodes.label: Row state hierarchy default<hover<selected (selected survives hover); sort indicators; column alignment by content type
nodes.norm_label: row state hierarchy default<hover<selected (selected survives hover); sort indicators; column alignment by content type

nodes.label: One font family, four weights (400/500/600/700), sentence case everywhere, ALL CAPS never for UI text
nodes.norm_label: one font family, four weights (400/500/600/700), sentence case everywhere, all caps never for ui text

nodes.label: Error reconciliation policy
nodes.rationale: Classifies every non-2xx response into exactly one of auth/transient/deterministic buckets so a network hiccup can never silently discard an optimistic local write — only an explicit server rejection or local delete removes it.

nodes.label: Parallel Fan-Out write model
nodes.rationale: Local store write and remote dispatch happen independently from the same synchronous handler so neither is gated on the other, making a store-only (offline) coordinator a first-class supported configuration rather than a degraded fallback.

nodes.label: Presenter / Binder Split
nodes.rationale: Presenters (computed display fields) are registered on the store; the coordinator stays a pure binder that transports already-decorated records without knowing their shape, keeping view-binding decoupled from data shaping.

nodes.label: Sync ownership
nodes.rationale: The coordinator, not the store, decides WHEN to sync (init/online/visibility) via one shared module-level listener set, keeping the store free of visibility/online listeners of its own.

nodes.label: No pending/rollback state model
nodes.rationale: A record is a record — optimistic mutations apply unconditionally with no snapshot/rollback machinery, pushing all confirm/revert reconciliation responsibility onto the coordinator.

nodes.label: Windowed Residency (Virtualization)
nodes.rationale: Caps resident records via a position-to-id index keyed to the server's authoritative order, so a huge dataset never overwhelms IndexedDB/memory while a locally created unpositioned record is never evicted.

nodes.label: Master anti-pattern list spanning components, layout, and completeness gaps
nodes.norm_label: master anti-pattern list spanning components, layout, and completeness gaps

nodes.label: Per-component mandatory feature table: Data Table, Form, Modal, Tabs, Search, Status Badge, Empty State, Loading State, KPI Card
nodes.norm_label: per-component mandatory feature table: data table, form, modal, tabs, search, status badge, empty state, loading state, kpi card

nodes.label: A component is not done until it has all its standard features
nodes.norm_label: a component is not done until it has all its standard features
nodes.rationale: An incomplete component is a broken component — a table without sort/filter/search/virtual-scroll is a prototype, not a table; a form without validation/loading/error handling is a sketch, not a form.

nodes.label: Decision tree: stat card vs data table vs card grid vs nav list vs activity feed vs form vs tabs
nodes.norm_label: decision tree: stat card vs data table vs card grid vs nav list vs activity feed vs form vs tabs

nodes.label: Admin/internal (max density) vs client-facing (moderate) vs public dashboard (focused density) design contexts
nodes.norm_label: admin/internal (max density) vs client-facing (moderate) vs public dashboard (focused density) design contexts

nodes.label: Lead with the answer; group related data; progressive disclosure; one primary metric per card
nodes.norm_label: lead with the answer; group related data; progressive disclosure; one primary metric per card

nodes.label: 7-step process: purpose → data → layout → components → completeness → states → flow
nodes.norm_label: 7-step process: purpose → data → layout → components → completeness → states → flow

nodes.label: Dense but readable: no empty decoration, compact spacing, numeric alignment, truncate with access
nodes.norm_label: dense but readable: no empty decoration, compact spacing, numeric alignment, truncate with access

nodes.label: Page type decision table: dashboard/list/detail/form/settings → layout
nodes.norm_label: page type decision table: dashboard/list/detail/form/settings → layout

nodes.label: Table for comparable tabular data (4+ attributes); card grid for visually distinct self-contained items
nodes.norm_label: table for comparable tabular data (4+ attributes); card grid for visually distinct self-contained items

nodes.label: Every component must address default/hover/focus/active/disabled/loading/empty/error visual states
nodes.norm_label: every component must address default/hover/focus/active/disabled/loading/empty/error visual states

nodes.label: One focal point per section; primary action stands alone; labels lighter than values
nodes.norm_label: one focal point per section; primary action stands alone; labels lighter than values

nodes.label: Platform-First Execution philosophy
nodes.rationale: Hooks directly into the browser's native layout engine (reset to auto, read scrollHeight) instead of introducing heavy observers or layouts.

nodes.label: Format resolution (Intl + custom tokens)
nodes.rationale: Empty or keyword values resolve to Intl.DateTimeFormat while anything else is a custom ICU-style pattern, letting authors choose locale-correct display without hand-rolling formatting.

nodes.label: Formatter caching pattern
nodes.rationale: Caches Intl formatters keyed by locale+options to avoid reconstruction cost on every format call.

nodes.label: Locale detection via nearest [lang]
nodes.rationale: Walking up the DOM to the nearest lang attribute (falling back to navigator.language) lets a single page host mixed-locale regions without a global setting.

nodes.label: Programmatic set interceptor (defineProperty)
nodes.rationale: Wrapping hidden.value via Object.defineProperty keeps the native picker's state consistent with a script-driven change without a separate setter API.

nodes.label: Typed input parsing (locale separator inference)
nodes.rationale: Dot/slash/dash separators map to European/US/ISO date conventions so users can type dates in their own regional format without a picker.

nodes.label: Native submit, always
nodes.rationale: Forms must carry a real action/method so they degrade gracefully without JS; PUT/DELETE ride POST via a Laravel-style _method spoofing input rather than ln-form serializing or dispatching submit itself.

nodes.label: Populate, don't orchestrate
nodes.rationale: ln-form keeps no validation state and no submit-button logic — it only writes values and dispatches synthetic input/change events, leaving submission and validation ownership entirely to other components.

nodes.label: RESTful action routing (create vs edit)
nodes.rationale: Rewrites form.action and the hidden _method input off the fill record so Laravel REST backends get create-vs-edit routing with no coordinator JS or extra click listener.

nodes.label: Transport Gateway pattern
nodes.rationale: Isolates networking concerns completely so the cache store and presentation layers stay fully network-agnostic.

nodes.label: Confirm-before-leaving interstitial composition
nodes.rationale: Composes ln-modal with a capture-phase click listener that must run before ln-external-links' bubble-phase :clicked dispatch, since :clicked is a notification, not a cancelable hook, and cannot stop navigation itself.

nodes.label: Double-Fill Prevention for hash-bound triggers
nodes.rationale: A hash-bound anchor trigger is ignored by ln-fill's own click listener and delegated entirely to ln-ui-coordinator, preventing redundant parallel fill operations from firing twice on the same click.

nodes.label: Composing with data-ln-modal-for
nodes.rationale: ln-fill deliberately never calls preventDefault(), so one button can carry both data-ln-fill-form and data-ln-modal-for and both independent document listeners fire on the same click.

nodes.label: Reserved suffixes (form, store)
nodes.rationale: form and store dataset suffixes are excluded from the built record so routing metadata never leaks into the filled data payload.

nodes.label: Targeted dispatch addressing model
nodes.rationale: Dispatching directly at the addressed element makes the DOM tree itself the routing infrastructure, avoiding the cost every fillable would pay under a document-broadcast-and-filter model, and enabling containment addressing (fill everything inside a modal) that flat id-broadcast cannot express.

nodes.label: Attribute Bridge
nodes.rationale: The attribute is the single source of truth; any external code can trigger the same state change and get identical behaviour, so the component never has two code paths to the same state.

nodes.label: Attribute IS the state (no imperative setter)
nodes.norm_label: attribute is the state (no imperative setter)
nodes.rationale: There is no setValue()/setMax() imperative API; el.setAttribute(...) is the canonical update path, keeping the attribute the sole source of truth.

nodes.label: Synchronous localStorage rationale
nodes.rationale: Unlike async network databases, ln-autosave uses browser localStorage so drafts are written instantly on field blur/leave, eliminating race conditions during page changes.

nodes.label: Active state tracking via selectionchange
nodes.rationale: Re-queries queryCommandState and DOM ancestry on every selectionchange instead of caching formatting state, keeping toolbar aria-pressed state always correct without stale-cache bugs.

nodes.label: Link Popover authored-template pattern
nodes.rationale: The editor never generates the link-input popover markup itself; requiring an authored <template> keeps the popover fully customizable and localizable in HTML.

nodes.label: Paste sanitization
nodes.rationale: Recursively strips disallowed tags/attributes from pasted HTML (e.g. from Word) to a safe whitelist, preventing unsafe markup injection from external sources.

nodes.label: Progressive enhancement (textarea fallback)
nodes.rationale: Without JS the underlying textarea still works as plain text, so the enhancement never blocks basic functionality.

nodes.label: The Attribute Bridge Pattern
nodes.rationale: The DOM is the single source of truth: prototype methods write attributes only, the shared observer reads them back into sync(), so programmatic mutation behaves identically to editing attributes in devtools.

nodes.label: Configuration Attributes vs Control-State Attributes
nodes.rationale: Typed config attributes should not be parsed once and cached on the instance, since that copy can drift from the DOM; read them live instead.

nodes.label: Custom Namespace Recommendation
nodes.rationale: Project-specific components should use their own prefix instead of data-ln-* to avoid future naming collisions with core library updates.

nodes.label: defineAttrs / attrInt / attrBool / attrList Helpers
nodes.rationale: Installed properties are getter-only because nothing is copied into instance state — there is no cached value to invalidate.

nodes.label: The Teardown Contract (destroy())
nodes.rationale: Every component must fully clean up pools, observers, listeners and DOM instance refs on destroy() to prevent memory leaks.

nodes.label: First Component: Collapsible Sidebar via data-ln-toggle
nodes.norm_label: first component: collapsible sidebar via data-ln-toggle

nodes.label: html lang Attribute Localization Requirement
nodes.rationale: Number, date and time components auto-localize via browser Intl APIs keyed off the html lang attribute.

nodes.label: MutationObserver Auto-Initialization
nodes.rationale: Adding a data-ln-* attribute in devtools immediately starts the component with no manual init call, because the global observer scans reactively.

nodes.label: Form is an interactive conversation: keyup validation from first keystroke, no layout shift
nodes.norm_label: form is an interactive conversation: keyup validation from first keystroke, no layout shift

nodes.label: Validation constraints use native HTML attributes (required, type=email, minlength, pattern)
nodes.norm_label: validation constraints use native html attributes (required, type=email, minlength, pattern)

nodes.label: Anti-pattern: disabling submit button until form is valid
nodes.norm_label: anti-pattern: disabling submit button until form is valid
nodes.rationale: Prevents users from seeing why submit is blocked or what to fix.

nodes.label: Untouched required fields show no error on load; errors only after interaction
nodes.norm_label: untouched required fields show no error on load; errors only after interaction

nodes.label: Every input field validates instantly on keyup from first keystroke
nodes.norm_label: every input field validates instantly on keyup from first keystroke

nodes.label: Decision matrix: simple flat forms → modal, complex/conditional forms → page
nodes.norm_label: decision matrix: simple flat forms → modal, complex/conditional forms → page

nodes.label: Submit shows loading spinner + disables only while server request is pending
nodes.norm_label: submit shows loading spinner + disables only while server request is pending

nodes.label: Error message container occupies height in DOM even when hidden
nodes.norm_label: error message container occupies height in dom even when hidden
nodes.rationale: Prevents layout shift / page jumps when validation errors appear.

nodes.label: User input preserved on server error; forms never cleared on error
nodes.norm_label: user input preserved on server error; forms never cleared on error

nodes.label: Submit stays enabled; invalid submit blocks + shows inline errors + focuses first invalid field
nodes.norm_label: submit stays enabled; invalid submit blocks + shows inline errors + focuses first invalid field

nodes.label: Header(title+close, sticky) / Body(scrollable) / Footer(actions, one primary, sticky)
nodes.norm_label: header(title+close, sticky) / body(scrollable) / footer(actions, one primary, sticky)

nodes.label: Backdrop darkens page; clicking backdrop must not dismiss the modal
nodes.norm_label: backdrop darkens page; clicking backdrop must not dismiss the modal
nodes.rationale: Prevents accidental data loss from stray backdrop clicks.

nodes.label: Modal is an explicit interruption; <form> must be the root container
nodes.norm_label: modal is an explicit interruption; <form> must be the root container

nodes.label: Destructive confirm: error styling, default focus on Cancel, title names the consequence
nodes.norm_label: destructive confirm: error styling, default focus on cancel, title names the consequence

nodes.label: Modal content container MUST be wrapped in a <form> root element
nodes.norm_label: modal content container must be wrapped in a <form> root element

nodes.label: Four standard sizes: sm(~400px) md(~560px) lg(~720px) xl(~900px), by content requirement
nodes.norm_label: four standard sizes: sm(~400px) md(~560px) lg(~720px) xl(~900px), by content requirement

nodes.label: Focus trapped within modal while open; ESC closes the modal
nodes.norm_label: focus trapped within modal while open; esc closes the modal

nodes.label: Anti-pattern: spawning a modal on top of an existing open modal
nodes.norm_label: anti-pattern: spawning a modal on top of an existing open modal

nodes.label: Modals must not spawn child modals on top of themselves
nodes.norm_label: modals must not spawn child modals on top of themselves

nodes.label: Modal contents and input fields reset/normalized upon receiving open commands
nodes.norm_label: modal contents and input fields reset/normalized upon receiving open commands

nodes.label: Construction-time snapshot (originalText/confirmText)
nodes.rationale: Re-reading text per confirm would race AJAX-driven content updates and change the button text mid-confirm, so the contract is snapshotted once at construction.

nodes.label: Platform Event Release philosophy
nodes.rationale: Acceptance is the standard platform click event, not a custom accept handler — on the second click the component steps out of the way of the default action.

nodes.label: Console Observation Layer
nodes.rationale: Logs every ln-* event and data-ln-* attribute mutation to the console so the library's whole runtime life is visible on demand, without touching page-owned attributes like class/style/aria-*.

nodes.label: Console Warning Filter
nodes.rationale: Gates library warnings behind data-ln-debug so production stays silent and zero-overhead while dev mode surfaces broken references immediately.

nodes.label: Generic Cross-Reference Contract Verifier
nodes.rationale: Catches unresolved -for/-source/-store targets, duplicate stores, and attribute typos that would otherwise fail silently and waste debugging time.

nodes.label: Host containment
nodes.rationale: An event/mutation is logged only when an active data-ln-debug host .contains() the target, keeping this layer symmetric with every other component in the library — it observes only its own subtree.

nodes.label: Page-wide exception (window/document events)
nodes.rationale: A handful of dispatch() calls target window/document directly since no element subtree can contain a non-element target; these log only when document.body itself is a host.

nodes.label: Zero Production Overhead
nodes.rationale: Runs strictly in dev mode so shipped bundles pay no verification cost.

nodes.label: The Five Rules of Hash-State
nodes.rationale: Prevents components from clobbering each other's URL parameters when multiple overlays share one URL fragment.

nodes.label: Rule 2: Foreign-Segment Preservation
nodes.rationale: Direct literal writes to location.hash would clobber other components' segments; all writes must go through hashSet.

nodes.label: Navigation Path vs Component Hash State
nodes.norm_label: navigation path vs component hash state

nodes.label: Rule 5: Router Fragment Guard
nodes.rationale: Ignoring popstate transitions that differ only in the fragment lets the Back button dismiss open modals without tearing down the under-modal page view.

nodes.label: View Teardown and Open-Overlay Cleanup
nodes.rationale: Simply discarding elements would leave active listeners and orphaned top-layer overlays floating in memory; the router calls destroy() and closes open popovers rooted in the exiting region.

nodes.label: Form-Scope Priority Rule
nodes.rationale: data-ln-form-scope always takes priority over data-ln-ajax; a form cannot be both AJAX-driven and database-scoped.

nodes.label: Method Gating Rule (POST/PUT/PATCH only)
nodes.rationale: GET forms such as search filters must run natively, bypassing the local-first write pipeline entirely.

nodes.label: The Three Levels of Submit Interception
nodes.norm_label: the three levels of submit interception

nodes.label: Zero Coordinator JS Principle
nodes.rationale: Edit values are stamped declaratively via data-ln-fill-*/data-ln-modal-* on the trigger button, so no custom coordinator script is needed for a shared create/edit modal.

nodes.label: Form Division of Labor (Validate/Form/Coordinator)
nodes.rationale: A form is a form — no scoped/unscoped variants or per-method conditionals; ln-validate owns all validation, ln-form owns fill and action, and the coordinator claim owns transport.

nodes.label: Multi-Step Form Rules
nodes.rationale: Reserved for 3+ distinct phases, dependent steps, or commit-preview needs; under 10 fields stays a single form with sections.

nodes.label: Validation Behavior Rules (Keyup, Never Disabled Submit)
nodes.norm_label: validation behavior rules (keyup, never disabled submit)

nodes.label: Data table distinguishes empty(no data) vs empty(zero results)
nodes.norm_label: data table distinguishes empty(no data) vs empty(zero results)

nodes.label: CTA action must match the underlying cause (create vs reset/clear)
nodes.norm_label: cta action must match the underlying cause (create vs reset/clear)

nodes.label: Anti-pattern: same generic empty message for onboarding and zero-results
nodes.norm_label: anti-pattern: same generic empty message for onboarding and zero-results

nodes.label: Anti-pattern: omitting actionable CTA buttons from empty states
nodes.norm_label: anti-pattern: omitting actionable cta buttons from empty states

nodes.label: Data containers must never present a blank void without an empty state
nodes.norm_label: data containers must never present a blank void without an empty state

nodes.label: Type 1: No Data Exists — resource onboarding empty state
nodes.norm_label: type 1: no data exists — resource onboarding empty state
nodes.rationale: Resource dataset has 0 records total; goal is onboarding the user and guiding initial creation.

nodes.label: Type 2: Query Returned Zero — search/filter zero state
nodes.norm_label: type 2: query returned zero — search/filter zero state
nodes.rationale: Data exists in backend but the active filter/search returns 0 rows; goal is helping the user reset scope, not onboarding.

nodes.label: Empty states must not carry heavier visual weight than populated states
nodes.norm_label: empty states must not carry heavier visual weight than populated states

nodes.label: Search distinguishes 'no data exists' vs 'zero results' empty states
nodes.norm_label: search distinguishes 'no data exists' vs 'zero results' empty states

nodes.label: Hidden Input Sync for Form Submit
nodes.norm_label: hidden input sync for form submit

nodes.label: External-link hostname test
nodes.rationale: Truthy hostname + hostname !== location.hostname makes non-http(s) schemes resolve as internal automatically, since they parse to an empty hostname.

nodes.label: Global service pattern
nodes.rationale: No registerComponent, no consumer-facing opt-in attribute — it loads, runs once, and decorates every link on the page unconditionally, unlike per-element components.

nodes.label: Idempotency marker pattern
nodes.rationale: data-ln-external-link="processed" prevents double-decoration across repeated passes and doubles as an unofficial opt-out hatch when pre-authored, though this only works because of how the guard happens to be implemented.

nodes.label: MutationObserver-driven decoration
nodes.rationale: Watches document.body for childList and href-attribute changes so dynamically inserted or mutated links are decorated without any producer signaling the component.

nodes.label: navigation (sidebar/header nav)
nodes.rationale: Uses semantic nav/ul/li/a with h6 section headers and hr dividers instead of generic divs, with active state via aria-current or data-ln-nav.

nodes.label: Delta-Only Inheritance
nodes.rationale: Derived mixins add only what differs from the base so a base color change propagates automatically to variants; otherwise it's duplication, not inheritance.

nodes.label: One Component, One Definition
nodes.rationale: A recipe is applied to one shared selector; re-applying a mixin across bespoke selectors creates parallel definitions that drift apart over time.

nodes.label: Three-Tier Stylesheet Distribution
nodes.rationale: Supports headless usage, custom brand themes, and turnkey apps from one build: core.css (zero tokens), theme.css (design tokens), full.css (combined).

nodes.label: Two-Layer SCSS Design System (Mixin vs Component)
nodes.norm_label: two-layer scss design system (mixin vs component)
nodes.rationale: Mixin layer holds pure style recipes; component layer binds them to selectors so consumer code applies mixins locally instead of copy-pasting rules.

nodes.label: Path A: CDN Installation
nodes.rationale: Always pin to a released tag rather than a moving branch so production builds stay reproducible.

nodes.label: Path C: Precompiled, Self-Hosted
nodes.rationale: demo/dist/ is committed to the repo so a clone gives working assets immediately with no runtime build step.

nodes.label: Sort Triggers Live in <ul data-ln-sort> in <th>
nodes.norm_label: sort triggers live in <ul data-ln-sort> in <th>
nodes.rationale: ln-table does not render sort buttons on its own; markup must author them.

nodes.label: SSR Hydration for Instant First Paint
nodes.norm_label: ssr hydration for instant first paint

nodes.label: data-ln-value Sort/Filter Primitive Rule
nodes.rationale: Sorting/filtering read the raw value from the universal data-ln-value attribute so formatted display text is never sorted.

nodes.label: Search Behavior Rule (No Debounce on Client Cache)
nodes.norm_label: search behavior rule (no debounce on client cache)
nodes.rationale: Array.filter on an in-memory cache is synchronous, so filtering on every keystroke needs no debounce; debounce only applies once search hits a server endpoint.

nodes.label: Anti-pattern: traditional pagination buttons instead of virtual scroll
nodes.norm_label: anti-pattern: traditional pagination buttons instead of virtual scroll
nodes.rationale: Conflicts with the viewport principle — users work with their entire dataset, not page-number slices.

nodes.label: Checkbox row selection with header select-all and bulk action bar
nodes.norm_label: checkbox row selection with header select-all and bulk action bar

nodes.label: Sticky footer: counts, aggregates, bulk actions
nodes.norm_label: sticky footer: counts, aggregates, bulk actions

nodes.label: Sticky header: per-column sort toggle + filter dropdown
nodes.norm_label: sticky header: per-column sort toggle + filter dropdown

nodes.label: Toolbar holds only search + primary create action
nodes.norm_label: toolbar holds only search + primary create action

nodes.label: Data table = viewport into dataset, not paginated slice
nodes.norm_label: data table = viewport into dataset, not paginated slice
nodes.rationale: Users work with entire dataset through a scrollable window; data resides in client-side cache so sort/filter/search operate synchronously while the system syncs with the server in the background.

nodes.label: Virtual scroll renders only visible rows + buffer from client cache
nodes.norm_label: virtual scroll renders only visible rows + buffer from client cache

nodes.label: Windowed table exception (data-ln-table-window)
nodes.rationale: For datasets too large to cache entirely client-side, the viewport principle holds but a bounded sliding window round-trips queries to the server as the user scrolls; sort/filter/search still resolve over the full dataset, computed server-side instead of locally.

nodes.label: Controls triggering active loading state must disable to prevent duplicate submissions
nodes.norm_label: controls triggering active loading state must disable to prevent duplicate submissions

nodes.label: Anti-pattern: full-page blocking loaders for localized element updates
nodes.norm_label: anti-pattern: full-page blocking loaders for localized element updates

nodes.label: At-Rest AES-GCM Encryption
nodes.rationale: Keeps the record id in plaintext so IndexedDB index lookups still work while encrypting the rest of the payload, balancing queryability against confidentiality of cached data.

nodes.label: Declarative State Model
nodes.rationale: No imperative state-change methods exist; external scripts must set input.checked and dispatch a native change event, keeping the checkbox DOM as the single source of truth.

nodes.label: Decoupled Two-Host Bridge
nodes.rationale: Dispatches a cancelable ln-filter:change so a consumer like ln-table (SSR) or ln-data-store can preventDefault() to claim filtering and skip the component's own default DOM-hiding behavior.

nodes.label: Sentinel Rules (mutual exclusion / collapse)
nodes.rationale: Keeps the reset ("All") checkbox always in a valid state — checking it clears values, unchecking the last value re-checks it, and checking every value auto-collapses to it — so an empty selection is never reachable.

nodes.norm_label: tab headers may show count badges; active tab uses high-contrast visual indicator

nodes.label: Three Sanctioned Coordinator Input Forms (§4.1)
nodes.rationale: When an operation has no attribute form, the coordinator must use one of request-{action}, set-{noun}, or {outcome} event grammars rather than inventing ad hoc event names.

nodes.label: The Four Data Concerns (Data/Render/Submit/Validate)
nodes.rationale: Concerns interact only via events, never by directly querying another concern's private state, keeping storage/rendering/submission/validation independently replaceable.

nodes.label: The Write Loop (optimistic + reconciliation)
nodes.rationale: Parallel fan-out to local cache and transport lets the UI update instantly; id-swap rekey on server confirmation and deterministic 4xx/409/5xx handling keep the cache consistent without blocking the user.

nodes.label: Offline Queue FIFO Retry & Auth Pause
nodes.norm_label: offline queue fifo retry & auth pause
nodes.rationale: Per-chain FIFO ordering with id-remap before ack prevents out-of-order updates against a temp ID; exponential backoff (2s..300s) with pause-after-8-failures and 401/419 auth pauses keep optimistic writes visible while the user re-authenticates.

nodes.label: Optimistic & Offline Write Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Direct pipeline (queue absent) and persistent offline pipeline (queue present) both intercept native submit at document level and write optimistically to IndexedDB before transport, so UI updates never wait on the network.

nodes.label: URL Hash State Synchronization (data-ln-hash)
nodes.rationale: Each component owns exactly one hash namespace and strictly preserves foreign segments during mutation; boot priority is URL hash > localStorage persist > authored markup, so deep links win over cached session state.
